title: Fast surge isolation + credential containment scratchpad
body:
Context:
This is a working scratchpad for a quick containment pattern we trialed during the Nov 2 rapid surge event. The objective: limit blast radius when an API key leaks or a sudden credential stuffing / automated client flood hits endpoints that consume large token budgets (streaming completions + embeddings). This is intentionally conversational and action-oriented — keep the oncall flow short and testable.

Top-level approach (fast containment):
- Detect anomaly -> carve isolation slices -> throttle/redirect -> rotate/issue ephemeral creds -> follow-up telemetry + comms.
- Prioritize maintaining customer-facing success for unaffected tenants while reducing global tail latency and cost.

Telemetry signals we used (ordered by signal-to-noise):
- per-api-key request rate (rps) 1m/5m windows + sudden delta > 10x baseline
- per-customer token consumption 1m delta and 1h sustained burn rate
- high error mix (4xx/401 + 429) + concurrent bursts of long streaming sessions
- WAF signature triggers aggregated per-src ASN or /24 prefix
- Downstream cost spike alerts (unusual GPU utilization + model token/sec)

Quick oncall run actions (playbook-lite):
1) Scoped visibility (2 min)
   - Run: kubectl exec -it telemetry-api -- curl \"http://localhost:8080/metrics?key=<key>\" or query metrics engine: rate(api.requests{api_key=\"<key>\"}[1m])
   - Find top-5 keys by tokens/min and identify associated tenant ids (if mapping exists). If mapping missing, escalate to identity-mapping oncall.
2) Immediate isolation (3–5 min)
   - If single key: issue temporary soft-block on key with TTL 15m (flag in rate-limiter middleware). Reason: avoid full key revocation before customer contact.
     Command (example): POST /admin/keys/<key>/flags {\"soft_block\":true, \"ttl\":\"15m\", \"reason\":\"suspected-leak-autothrottle\"}
   - If many keys from same tenant and tenant is suspicious: move tenant to emergency-quota profile (derive from tenant baseline * 0.2) via config update: PUT /config/tenants/<tenant>/quota {\"burst\":50, \"sustained\":10}
   - If flood originates from a source ASN or IP block: temp WAF rule to drop or challenge (Cloud WAF / ModSecurity): add rule id waf-temp-<timestamp> with low-latency drop on sig-match.
3) Containment with graceful UX (5–10 min)
   - For keys soft-blocked, return 401 + body {\"error\":\"temporarily_throttled\",\"support\":\"https://...\"} to avoid indefinite retries and reduce downstream load.
   - For tenant-level throttles: return 429 with Retry-After header per usual. Add header X-RW-Containment: rapid-surge-<id> for tracing.
4) Credential lifecycle ops (10–30 min)
   - Rotate leaked key(s) if confirmed; otherwise keep soft-block for contact window. Run: POST /admin/keys/<key>/rotate -> new_key returned -> stage for customer support release.
   - Issue ephemeral read-only keys for customers who need to continue essential traffic (e.g., single-route allowance). TTL: 1h.
5) Re-routing & model fallback (10+ min)
   - Route unknown heavy streams to cheaper, lower-capacity model with strict token caps via routing rules: route(policy=containment) -> model=small-quantized-1; also enable streaming truncation at 512 tokens.
6) Observe for 30–60 min then deescalate or escalate to full revocation/blacklist/incident.

WAF tuning notes (practical heuristics):
- Avoid broad IP blocks early. Prefer behavioral WAF rules: signature == repeated fast POSTs to /v1/complete with similar prompt fingerprint or identical header patterns.
- Use header fingerprinting: UA + Accept-Language + X-RW-Client-Id hashed. When > 5k identical requests in 1m -> create temporary challenge for that fingerprint.
- When source is clearly a credential stuffing botnet: combine rate-limiter keyed by IP and key, then escalate to block for 6h with review.

Rate limiter patterns used during exercise:
- Multilevel keys: global default, tenant, key. Policy evaluation order: key -> tenant -> global. Each policy can set burst (tokens) and sustained.
- Emergency partitioning: create \"emergency-iso-<id>\" bucket and move offending key's traffic there with lower CPU/IO priority (nice-ish) so it doesn't starve others.
- Continuous-batching knob: reduce batch_wait_ms for affected worker pools to 0 to avoid batching long-latency streams into healthy workloads.

Example gating rule (pseudo):
- If tokens/min(key) > baseline(key)*10 AND tokens/min(key) > 5000 -> place in emergency-iso, soft-block TTL 15m, route rest to fallback-model, tag traces with containment-id.

Observability + investigation checklist:
- Capture sample of offending payloads (first 100 requests) and store in secure S3 with redaction. Label: containment-<id>/samples/
- Correlate with support tickets and recent key rotations for that tenant.
- Check recent ACLs and terraform changes in infra repo for abnormal deploys linked to key ownership.
- Save flamegraphs of affected worker pods and tokenization distribution.

Customer comms template (short):
Subject: Temporary service limitation on your API key
Body: \"We detected unusual activity originating from one of your API keys and temporarily limited traffic to protect your account and our service. We will hold the key in a temporary containment state for up to 15 minutes while we investigate. If you believe this is expected traffic, reply with the relevant ticket id and we will restore capacity. If compromised, we will rotate the key and share a new credential.\n\nWhat to expect: limited request throughput, 401/429 responses for affected calls, and a follow-up from SRE or Support within 1 hour.\"

Post-incident follow-ups / experiments to run (backlog):
- Test ephemeral-key flow automation: ensure support can auto-issue 1h allowlist keys via internal console without full rotation.
- Improve key -> tenant mapping latency (goal: <30s) so oncall can always map offending key to owner quickly.
- Run tabletop sim: simulate concurrent leaks of 3 keys from 3 tenants and measure mean latency for healthy tenants.
- Add autotriage ML model: classify request clusters by prompt hash to group likely attacks vs legit spikes.

Known limitations & open questions:
- Soft-block observable: if attackers rotate keys frequently, TTLs are ineffective. Need ability to ban by fingerprint cluster not just key.
- WAF false positives: some legitimate SDKs might have identical UA combos. Need to allowlist verified SDK hashes.
- Impact on billing: emergency-quota adjustments will affect cost reports; need billing-safe labels to avoid overcharging customers during containment windows.

Operational notes for next drill:
- Assign roles explicitly: detector (metrics person), containment lead (applies soft-blocks), comms (customer support draft), infra (WAF / firewall ops).
- Pre-create scripts for: soft-block key, assign tenant emergency quota, create fallback route, and create containment S3 bucket + upload script. Store in infra runbook repo.

References / links:
- SRE-879 (jira): postmortem checklist for Nov 2 surge
- infra PR 512: emergency-iso bucket implementation
- CON-1234: customer communication playbook

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add exact API endpoints for each internal admin action to infra runbook (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Create post-incident billing label automation (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Run the tabletop with at least 2 SREs + 1 support engineer before EoQ (owner: Priya)

Notes to self: keep containment-id as UUID-like timestamp for cross-system joins. When in doubt start with soft-block + limited TTL; full revocation requires product approval unless key is confirmed exfiltrated.

End of scratchpad.
